The original description (Light 1935, Proc. Calif. Acad. Sci. 4th ser. 21(20): 233–258) could not be obtained locally (archive.org lacks that volume), so the revision is cited; per Bacchus the holotype soldier comes from Charles Island, Galápagos, and was not examined. Localities, material examined, figures and biological notes are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate is close to C. brevis and C. kirbyi; all three lack an arolium between the tarsal claws, but in this species the head length to the lateral base of the mandibles is 0.86–0.94 mm and the hind tibia 0.75–0.81 mm, both outside the comparable ranges of C. brevis (1.00–1.17 mm, 0.88–1.09 mm) and C. kirbyi (1.00–1.09 mm head, with a shorter hind tibia of 0.68–0.78 mm). The soldier head index (length of head to cephalic ridge 1 divided by maximum head width) is 1.18–1.25, larger than the 0.95–1.16 of close relatives; the head is markedly constricted at the antennal sockets, the frontal and genal horns are squat and short, and the dorsal surface is very rugose and tuberculate.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text:
Head capsule yellowish-brown to reddish-brown posteriorly, dull yellow anteriorly, with a dark V-shaped band across the eyes behind the frons; clypeus yellow-white; antennae and labrum yellow; pronotum and abdominal tergites yellowish-brown, paler than or concolorous with the head, with a T-shaped mark near the anterior margin of the pronotum; sternites and legs yellow; wings faintly tinged with brown, darker from the costal margin to the radial sector.
The head capsule is noticeably shorter than the maximum width across the eyes, its posterior margin sharply rounded behind the eyes; the cranial suture is distinct; eyes and ocelli are oval to nearly round, the ocelli touching the eyes; antennae with 15 segments, segments 1 and 2 cylindrical, 1 longer than 2, 2 equal to 3, segment 4 smaller. Pronotum width narrower than the head width across the eyes; anterior margin widely and shallowly concave, sides rounded, posterior margin slightly emarginate. Fore wing with only the costal, radius and radial sector sclerotised; radial sector with four simple forward branches to the costa; media extending to the wing tip and sending up several vertical branches to the radial sector. Arolium absent.
Measurements (four specimens from three nest series; mean in parentheses): head length to lateral base of mandibles 0.86–0.94 mm (0.89), maximum width of head with eyes 1.01–1.04 mm (1.02), maximum length of labrum 0.10–0.18 mm (0.15), maximum width of labrum 0.39–0.42 mm (0.41), maximum diameter of compound eye 0.27–0.31 mm (0.30), minimum diameter of compound eye 0.27–0.29 mm (0.28), maximum diameter of lateral ocellus 0.10–0.12 mm (0.11), minimum diameter of lateral ocellus 0.08–0.10 mm (0.09), minimum ocellus/antennal distance 0.17–0.18 mm (0.17), minimum eye/antennal distance 0.05–0.07 mm (0.06), minimum distance of eye from lateral base of head 0.12–0.14 mm (0.13), maximum length of pronotum 0.55–0.64 mm (0.60), median length of pronotum 0.52–0.55 mm (0.53), maximum width of pronotum 0.86–0.94 mm (0.91), length of hind tibia 0.75–0.81 mm (0.78), length of fore wing scale 0.83–0.86 mm (0.84).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text:
Posterior and lower sides of the head capsule and the anterior margin of the pronotum yellowish-brown; frons and interior of the head black; antennae pale yellow; labrum, body and legs yellow; mandibles very dark reddish-brown.
In dorsal view the head is relatively long and narrow, widest about the frontal ridge, weakly constricted about the level of the antennal sockets; the sides below the antennal sockets splay outwards; the mid-vertex region bears a conspicuously large concavity; dorsal and lateral surfaces very rugose, tuberculated. Frontal ridge prominent, rough, produced forward, broadly and shallowly V-shaped with a median groove, recurved above the antennal sockets. Frons almost vertical, weakly rugose. Postclypeus with a prominent convex anterior margin. Labrum fleshy. Frontal horns larger and longer than the genal horns. Eyes oval, unpigmented and prominent. Antennae with 13–14 segments, segment 3 narrowest, slightly sclerotised, often incompletely separated from 4. Mandibles short and broad, dentition weakly developed. Pronotum generally wider than the head, anterior margin smooth, deeply and broadly concave, sides convex, postero-lateral corners rounded, posterior margin shallowly convex.
Measurements (10 specimens from five nest series; mean in parentheses): head length to lateral base of mandibles 0.86–1.04 mm (0.95), height of head excluding postmentum 0.81–0.96 mm (0.88), length of head to cephalic ridge 1 1.27–1.43 mm (1.38), length of head to cephalic ridge 2 1.07–1.30 mm (1.18), maximum width of head 1.11–1.20 mm (1.14), maximum length of labrum 0.08–0.13 mm (0.11), maximum width of labrum 0.18–0.29 mm (0.26), maximum length of pronotum 0.68–0.83 mm (0.77), median length of pronotum 0.60–0.73 mm (0.66), maximum width of pronotum 1.09–1.25 mm (1.17), maximum width of mesonotum 0.96–1.20 mm (1.04), maximum width of metanotum 1.01–1.22 mm (1.07), length of hind tibia 0.62–0.78 mm (0.71), length of left mandible 0.55–0.57 mm (0.56), left mandible, apical to first marginal 0.09–0.13 mm (0.10), left mandible, first to third marginal 0.08–0.13 mm (0.10), right mandible, apical to first marginal 0.10–0.16 mm (0.14), right mandible, first to second marginal 0.08–0.10 mm (0.08).
